MIND. [1] [Brom.]
Aversion to any kind of work, even reading ; takes no interest in household duties.
She does not feel as she generally does, but can't tell why.
Great depression of spirits. θ Scirrhus mamma.
Very much depressed and inconsolable. θ Cancer of mamma.
Very low-spirited, with pain in left iliac region.
Sad, discouraged. θ Swelling to testicle.
She is not like herself ; despondent, sits alone in her room without doing anything ; looks constantly in one direction without saying anything.
Violent coughing spells, with anxiety. θ Croup.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Brom.]
Headache deep in crown of head, with palpitation.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Brom.]
Scalp tender ; covered with an eruption, with dirty looking and offensive smelling discharge. θ Eczema.
Malignant scald head.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Brom.]
Throbbing stitches in left upper lid, extending to brow, forehead and left temple ; < by external pressure, motion and stooping ; > by rest ; pain unfits him for work.
Lachrymation of right eye, with swelling of lachrymal gland. θ Fistula lachrymalis.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Brom.]
Parotids, mostly left, affected. θ After scarlatina.
Swelling and hardness of left parotid gland, swelling feeling warm to touch. θ Sequel to scarlatina.
Suppuration of left parotid, edges of opening smooth ; discharge watery and excoriating ; swelling remaining hard and unyielding. θ After scarlatina. See 44.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Brom.]
Fanlike motion of nostrils.
Bleeding of nose, relieving chest.
Fluent coryza, with frequent violent sneezing ; corrosive soreness under nose and on margins of nose.
Yearly cold, with sore nostril and difficult breathing.
Fluent coryza, in which right nostril is more affected and more stopped.
Long-continued, obstinate coryza, with soreness beneath nose and on margin of nose ; also catarrh in fauces.
Whole nose sore, and wings of nose swollen ; a scurf forms in it, with pain and bleeding on wiping it.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Brom.]
Cancerous ulcer between right eye and ear, of size of palm of a child's hand.
Face of a bluish tinge, turning purplish at each effort to cough. θ Croup.
Grey ; earthy color of face ; oldish appearance. θ Cancer of mamma.
Face ashy grey. θ Diphtheria.
Cheeks sunken. θ Diphtheria.
Heat of face and head. θ Spasm of glottis.
Pale, collapsed face. θ Croup.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Brom.]
Slight swelling of articulation of left jaw, with cracking in it when chewing ; swelling and hardness of left parotid, which is warm to touch ; rosy-red swelling of tonsils and difficult swallowing ; tension and pressure when swallowing and when not ; pain in throat is especially < when swallowing fluids ; hawking up mucus.
Left submaxillary gland swollen to size of a small hen's egg, hard, not sore to pressure ; neighboring glands more or less similarly affected.
Stony, hard swelling of glands, especially on lower jaw and throat.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Brom.]
Fetor oris. θ Diphtheria.
Sensation of dryness and burning in mouth. θ Nasal catarrh.
Mouth dry and parched. θ Eczema.
Salivation increases and exudation decreases. θ Diphtheria.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Brom.]
Dryness in throat. θ Croup.
Scraping in throat, and a rough, deep voice, continued for an hour.
Swelling of mucous membrane of fauces and pharynx.
Small follicles in posterior fauces ; inflammation extending to larynx, causing a titillating cough.
Tonsils swollen, inflamed ; constant pain in throat, swallowing difficult, of fluids worse than solids. θ After measles.
Malignant forms of diphtheria.
Diphtheritis of larynx, or croup. [Obs. With apparent great sagacity one of our best authors says : "Bromine could not be a remedy in diphtheria and also in croup, as diphtheritis and croup are two diseases entirely different in their nature and character ; a chief croup remedy cannot at the same time be a great diphtheritis remedy, because a drug has not only to cover the symptoms, but must likewise correspond to the character of the disease." He quotes Belladonna : "Do we give Bellad. for headache in the full-blooded and robust and also in the bloodless and feeble ?" We answer, yes, we do frequently. Every fully proved drug has produced such "opposite" states and also cured them, if only the other symptoms, particularly the characteristics, correspond to the case. We have nothing to do with the disease, only with the sick and the characteristics of each case. --C. Hg.]
After all other symptoms have passed off, great weakness and lassitude. θ Diphtheria.
In cases where membrane forms back almost over larynx, Bromium removed husky tone of voice in a few hours. θ Diphtheria.
Preference for left side of throat. θ Diphtheritis.
Stiffness of neck with diphtheritis.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Brom.]
Desire for acids. θ Diarrhœa.
Aversion to customary tobacco smoking ; it causes nausea and vertigo. θ Diarrhœa.
   

EATING AND DRINKING. [15] [Brom.]
After eating, nausea and pains in stomach better. θ Diarrhœa.
Contractive spasm of stomach passing off after eating. θ Diarrhœa.
Gastric symptoms better from black coffee. θ Diarrhœa.
After a meal, diarrhœa.
After acids : diarrhœa ; cough worse.
After eating oysters, diarrhœa.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Brom.]
Nausea. θ Diarrhœa.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Brom.]
Emptiness of stomach. θ Diarrhœa.
Feeling of emptiness in stomach ; better after eating, for which, however, he had no longing.
Feeling of heaviness in stomach. θ Inflammation of stomach.
Pressure in stomach, like from a stone. θ Emphysema.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Brom.]
Enlargement and induration of spleen. θ After maltreated gonorrhœa.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Brom.]
Off and on a very strong pain and sore feeling in lower l. part of abdomen. θ Mental derangement.
Periodically much pain in left hypochondriac and iliac regions ; pain is violent, as if there were sore spots inside. θ Mental derangement.
Tympanitic distension of abdomen, and passage of much wind.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Brom.]
Croup of colon.
Black, fecal stools.
Diarrhœa after every meal ceases, but returns after oysters.
Blind, painful hemorrhoids during and after stool ; < from cold or warm water ; > from wetting with saliva.
Blind, intensely painful varices, with black, diarrheic stools.
Varices < from application of cold and warm water. θ Diarrhœa.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Brom.]
High-colored urine. θ Eczema.
   

MALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [22] [Brom.]
Swelling of testicle, remaining after gonorrhœa three months ago, size of a hen's egg, oval round, somewhat hard, not very sensitive to pressure, smooth ; pains most when driving ; Brom. [2] in water, three times daily, helped in three weeks, while working as a coachman.
Swelling of scrotum. θ Chronic gonorrhœa.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Brom.]
Continual dull pain in region of left ovary ; mild fluor albus ; no thrill in coition ; childless after eight years marriage ; strong woman, æt. 30 ; conception in three months.
Considerable pain in back and ovarian region. θ Mental derangement.
Constant, dull, boring pain in ovary. θ Dropsy.
Swelling and hardness of left ovary.
Uterus descends about 2 inches. θ Mental derangement.
Menses too early and too profuse ; bright red blood ; passive flow with much exhaustion ; membranous shreds may pass.
Fulness in head and chest, with difficult respiration a few days before catamenia.
Indescribable, queer ill feeling all over, which makes her low-spirited, a few days before catamenia.
During menses : pain in abdomen and small of back ; abdominal cramps, with subsequent soreness in abdomen ; frontal pain, feeling as if eyes would drop out while stooping.
Suppression of menses. θ Scirrhus mamma.
Loud emission of flatus from vagina. θ Dysmenorrhœa.
Much itching in vagina. θ Mental derangement.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Brom.]
Stitch pains from mamma to axillæ, cannot bear pressure. θ Scirrhus.
Hard, uneven tumor in right mamma, firmly adherent to its surroundings, with lancinating pains ; < from least pressure and at night.
Cancer mamma, open, with swelling of axillary glands ; stitches and burning in indurated parts ; in alternation with Conium.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Brom.]
Hoarseness.
Chronic hoarseness.
After overheating, hoarse for six weeks ; morning, aphonic, until after long coughing, with a whistling sound, some phlegm comes up. θ Cold after overheating.
Husky tone of voice. θ Diphtheria.
Hoarseness several days ; rough, dry cough ; pain in larynx ; in sleep difficult (snoring) breathing ; jumping up for want of breath while eating and drinking ; inhalation with a rushing sound. θ Croup.
Hoarseness ; larynx painful ; barking, dry cough ; a long drawn out, buzzing inhalation ; hot, moist skin. θ Croup.
Hoarseness ; aphonia ; snoring inhalation ; no cough ; relapse, with barking cough ; rattling ; suffocation ; cold sweat. θ Croup.
Voice hardly audible. θ Croup.
Spasm in glottis.
Stenosis of glottis.
Laryngitis ; tracheitis.
On swallowing saliva a stitch in posterior portion of larynx, with a feeling of contraction.
Tickling in larynx, with irritation to cough ; constrictive sensation deep in throat and dry cough.
Constriction in larynx.
Sticking constriction in larynx.
Scraping and rawness in larynx, provoking cough.
Scraping in larynx provoking dry cough in evening.
Cold sensation in larynx, with cold feeling when inspiring, after breakfast ; > after shaving.
Sensation of coldness in larynx.
Constant sore pain in larynx. θ Cold after overheating.
Beginning in larynx, coming upward, with hoarse and croupy cough ; low pulse. θ Diphtheria.
First bronchia, then larynx ; slow cases of croup ; large tubes have been coughed up. θ Croup.
Sensation as if air tubes were full of smoke. θ Catarrh.
Rattling of mucus in larynx on coughing ; cough having a croupy sound. θ Diphtheria.
Rattling of mucus without choking. θ Emphysema.
Bronchia much irritated. θ Croup.
When disease commences in larynx and comes up into fauces, and in some cases in which it runs down into larynx, and produces a croupy cough, with much rattling of mucus. θ Diphtheria.
No choking in cough as there is in Hepar. θ Croup.
Much rattling in larynx during breathing, still more when coughing ; danger of suffocation from too much phlegm in larynx (Tart. em. has rattling lower down in chest). θ Croup.
Inspiration very difficult, larynx drawn down ; thorax not moving ; respiration frequent ; rattling ; sawing ; voice not audible. θ Croup.
Cough hoarse, crowing, suffocative ; breathing sawing, whistling ; face red, hot ; large drops on forehead ; < bending over ; scrofulous girl, æt. 5. θ Croup.
Croup : spasms of larynx ; suffocative cough ; hoarse, whistling, croupy sound, with great effort ; rattling, wheezing ; gasping, impeded respiration ; heat of face ; formation of a false membrane in larynx to trachea ; much rattling in larynx when coughing.
Membranous formation in larynx and trachea. θ Croup.
Membranous forming back almost over larynx. θ Diphtheria.
Croupous inflammation formed by exuberant growth of fungi. θ Diphtheria. See 13.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Brom.]
Oppression of breath immediately after taking it, with deep inspiration, together with a sensation as if he did not get enough air into chest, on account of which he elevates thorax and inspires forcibly.
Breathing frequent, rattling, sawing. θ Croup.
Deep, forcible inspiration is necessary, from time to time.
Inspiration very difficult ; larynx is drawn down ; thorax immovable. θ Croup.
Difficulty of breathing ; cannot inspire deep enough.
Sensation as if air passages were full of smoke.
Gasping and snuffing for breath, with wheezing and rattling in larynx. θ Spasm of glottis.
Constriction in chest, with some difficulty of breathing ; no cough. θ Mental derangement.
An asthma in a girl, æt. 16, had remained for ten years after measles, so that she was never able to walk rapidly nor ascend steps without being very much exhausted, disappeared after five doses of five globules of the 30th, which she took for proving.
Tightness of chest. θ Asthma.
Asthma < at night.
Asthma of sailors, as soon as they "go ashore."
   

COUGH. [27] [Brom.]
Rough, barking, croup-like cough, with suffocative feeling like sulphur smoke ; breathing painful ; gasping for air ; convulsions ; great weakness. θ Whooping cough.
Whooping cough, with croupish hoarseness of cough.
Symptoms of croup during whooping cough.
Much fatiguing cough, with scanty, difficult loosened sputa of white, whitish-yellow or yellow phlegm ; later also several times pure, dark, coagulated blood. θ Cold after overheating.
Difficult, whistling cough, with hoarseness. θ Croup.
Cough gets much < from dust or cold air. θ Cold after overheating.
Cough excited by : tickling in larynx ; scraping and rawness in larynx ; deep inspiration ; violent motion.
Cough, with sudden paroxysms of suffocation on swallowing ; respiration very short ; obliged to catch for breath.
Cough, with excruciating pain and anxiety ; purulent, sometimes bloody expectoration ; pulse 120 ; respiration 30 ; temperature 100. θ Phthisis.
Sputa not frequent.
Catarrhal cough.
   

INNER CHEST AND LUNGS. [28] [Brom.]
Stitches in chest ; inflammation of lungs, right side. θ Croup. θ Diphtheria.
Affections begin with bronchi and ascend to larynx.
Cutting pains running upward. θ Phthisis.
Hepatization of lower lobes. θ Pneumonia.
After much cough with loose, bluish, granular expectoration, attacks of dyspnœa for several days, breathing difficult, laborious, short ; cough becomes dry ; in region of stomach, pressure and tension ; breathing noisy ; skin bluish, especially on hands, asthma forces her to sit up in night ; sensation of being beaten all over. θ Emphysema.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Brom.]
Anxious feeling about heart. θ Mental derangement.
Unbearable, violent cutting, left side under last ribs, from below upward, as if it would kill her ; old woman. θ Ossification of valves.
Violent cardiac pain and palpitation, with headache deep in under crown of head ; lameness of left arm.
Cutting pains running upward. θ Heart disease.
Pulse very soft. θ Diphtheria.
Pulse small, weak, not countable. θ Croup.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Brom.]
A goitre, already increased to size of a hen's egg, with a girl, æt. 14, who had menstruated one year, blonde, lively temperament, delicate constitution, disappeared within 16 weeks ; 30th in water, twice a day.
An obstinate goitre, not changed by Iodium in substance, disappeared after Brom. 30th, in water, twice daily for three months.
Glands of neck much swollen. θ Eczema.
Two encysted tumors on both sides of neck.
   

UPPER LIMBS. [32] [Brom.]
Eruption on right elbow. θ Eczema.
Icy cold forearms. θ Diarrhœa.
Hands cold and moist.
Cold hands. θ Diarrhœa.
Drawing pain through left breast into left arm.
   

NERVES. [36] [Brom.]
Nervousness. θ Eczema.
Great weakness and lassitude after all the symptoms have passed off. θ Diphtheria.
Much prostration. θ Croup.
Fainting. θ Diphtheria.
Subject to hysterical attacks, with fits. θ Mental derangement.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Brom.]
Continued yawning with respiratory troubles ; child yawns frequently and is drowsy. θ Croup.
Very much inclined to sleep.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Brom.]
Desire for open air.
   

FEVER. [40] [Brom.]
Skin cool, covered with viscous sweat. θ Croup.
   

ATTACKS, PERIODICITY. [41] [Brom.]
Periodical pains. θ Scirrhus of mamma.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Brom.]
Suppuration of left parotid gland, edges of opening smooth, ulcer unhealthy, discharge watery and excoriating ; swelling remaining hard and unyielding. θ After scarlatina.
Tonsils swollen after measles.
Tuberculosis.
Scrofulous swelling of glands, several already in suppuration ; in water twice daily.
Enlargement of thyroid, in children with light hair, blue eyes and fair skin.
Swelling and induration of glands (thyroid testes, submaxillary, parotid).
Emaciation. θ Cancer of mamma.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Brom.]
Blue eyes ; light hair ; fair skin. θ Struma. θ Croup.
Children with thin, white, delicate skins, and very light hair and eyebrows. θ Croup. θ Diphtheria.
Blonde, red-cheeked, scrofulous girls.
Scrofulous boy, æt. 10, given up ; 5th day of croup.
Woman, æt. 25, scrofulous, not married, menstruated regularly. θ Mental derangement.
Woman, æt. 27, married four years and no children ; dark complexion and very lively temperament. θ Mental derangement.
Woman, æt. 35, losing too much blood every month ; had no children.
